summary: This work demonstrates high-precision quantum simulation of magnon spectra and interactions in a 2D XY spin-1/2 magnet using a 97-qubit hybrid analog-digital superconducting processor, achieving $g/(2\pi) \approx 9.7$ MHz coupling strength and characterizing both linear and nonlinear magnon response functions with median relative precision of $7 \times 10^{-3}$ in frequency and $7.8 \times 10^{-2}$ in decay rate. The technique combines Hamiltonian learning achieving $4.7 \times 10^{-4}$ per-qubit-per-cycle XEB errors with interleaved digital Z-gate excitation to isolate individual magnon modes, revealing mode-dependent decay rates enhanced near van Hove singularities and suppressed for edge-localized corner modes.
motivation: Precise control over quasi-particle excitations in quantum many-body systems is essential for understanding microscopic scattering mechanisms, yet existing quantum simulators struggle to achieve both high-fidelity state preparation and the local control needed to excite and probe specific modes with tunable energy densities.
method: A global gate protocol (GGP) prepares low-temperature states with controllable energy density in 6 ns, followed by analog evolution under a learned Hamiltonian. Interleaved digital Z-gates with 2 ns switching times excite individual magnon modes, enabling measurement of retarded Green's functions $\chi_\mu(t) = -iA\langle\psi_0|[\hat{b}_\mu(t), \hat{b}_\mu^\dagger(0)]|\psi_0\rangle$. Pump-probe and two-mode collision experiments isolate scattering pathways; MPS simulations fail at elevated temperatures due to volume-law entanglement.
result: Temperature-dependent decay rates $\Gamma \propto (\epsilon - \epsilon_0)^\eta$ with $\eta \approx 0.7$ for high-energy modes reflect self-consistent broadening effects. Corner modes show $\sim 10$ times longer lifetimes than bulk modes; all four corner modes scatter exclusively into each other, forming a decoupled manifold. Nonlinear decay $\alpha_2$ scales as $A^2$ and exhibits negative temperature sensitivity at high energies, distinct from linear decay $\alpha_1$.
